title: Midnight Snack
desc: Street food origins, fermentation mysteries & flavour combos that shouldn't work

questions.q: Fish and chips was brought to England by immigrants from which two countries?
questions.a: Jewish refugees from Portugal and Spain — fried fish was a Sephardic Jewish tradition

questions.q: What common kitchen ingredient is chemically almost identical to TNT?
questions.a: Trinitrotoluene and sugar both contain carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen — but the real answer is that baking soda and vinegar's violent reaction is often confused with this. The actual answer: nothing common is close to TNT. Trick question!

questions.q: Korma, tikka masala, and balti were all invented in which country?
questions.a: Britain — they're British-Indian dishes, not traditional Indian cuisine

questions.q: What fruit smells so terrible it's banned on public transport in Singapore?
Ranch dressing was invented on an actual ranch. Where?
questions.a: Sweetwater Ranch in Santa Barbara, California — by Steve Henson in the 1950s

questions.q: Processed cheese was invented in Switzerland — true or false?
questions.a: True — Walter Gerber created it in 1911 to prevent cheese from spoiling during export

questions.q: What popular drink was accidentally invented by a pharmacist trying to cure headaches?
Why does pineapple make your mouth tingle and sting?
questions.a: It contains bromelain, an enzyme that literally digests the proteins in your mouth — the pineapple is eating you back

questions.q: Which country eats the most cheese per capita?
questions.a: Denmark (though France and Iceland are close behind)
